strings.city.0.p.0: A correct seating position is not only about comfort. It lets you control the car faster and more precisely, and the seat belt and airbags protect you as designed.
strings.city.0.list.0: Seat: with the brake (or clutch) pedal fully pressed, your leg remains slightly bent at the knee.
strings.city.0.list.1: Backrest: if you stretch out your arm, your wrist rests on the top of the steering wheel while your shoulders stay against the backrest.
strings.city.0.list.2: Head restraint: its top is roughly level with the top of your head and close to the back of your head.
strings.city.0.list.3: Hands on the wheel at “9 and 3 o’clock”.
strings.city.0.list.4: Interior mirror: you can see the whole rear window.
strings.city.0.list.5: Side mirrors: only a narrow strip of your own bodywork is visible, with the horizon roughly in the middle.
strings.city.0.list.6: Seat belt: the lap part low across the hips, the shoulder part across the middle of the shoulder, without twists. You and all passengers must be belted (para. 9(5) of the Rules).
strings.city.1.p.0: This is the basic habit for any manoeuvre: moving off, changing lanes, turning, making a U-turn and stopping. The order is always the same, and in time it becomes automatic.
strings.city.1.p.1: Signal before you begin the manoeuvre (para. 47 of the Rules). But an indicator only announces your intention: it gives you no priority and does not relieve you of the need for caution ⟦36⟧.
strings.city.1.list.0: Mirror: who is behind and beside you, and how fast they are going.
strings.city.1.list.1: Signal: switch the indicator on early enough for others to notice it.
strings.city.1.list.2: Mirror again, and a quick glance over your shoulder into the blind spot.
strings.city.1.list.3: Manoeuvre: smoothly, without jerking the wheel.
strings.city.1.list.4: After the manoeuvre, check that the indicator has switched off.
strings.city.2.p.0: When changing lanes, you give way to those travelling in the same direction without changing lane. If two cars change lanes at the same time, the one on the left gives way (para. 51 of the Rules).
strings.city.2.list.0: Pick a “gap” in the next lane and adjust your speed to it. Usually you need to speed up slightly rather than brake.
strings.city.2.list.1: Change one lane at a time, checking the mirrors each time.
strings.city.2.list.2: Take the lane for your turn in advance: before a turn you must take the appropriate far left or far right position ⟦37⟧.
strings.city.2.list.3: If you see no “gap”, it is better to drive on and turn round later than to squeeze in.
strings.city.2.list.4: Do not stay long next to another vehicle’s rear wing: there you are in its blind spot.
strings.city.3.p.0: A left turn is one of the most dangerous manoeuvres in town. When turning left or making a U-turn on a green signal, you give way to oncoming vehicles going straight or turning right (para. 95 of the Rules). At an intersection of roads of equal status the same rule applies ⟦38⟧, and you also give way to those approaching from the right ⟦39⟧.
strings.city.3.p.1: When turning in any direction, you give way to pedestrians crossing the road you are turning into ⟦40⟧.
strings.city.3.list.0: While you wait for a chance to turn, keep your wheels straight. If you are hit from behind, the car will not be pushed into the oncoming lane.
strings.city.3.list.1: Assess not only the first oncoming car but also those who may appear from behind it in the adjacent lane.
strings.city.3.list.2: Do not enter the intersection if there is a traffic jam beyond it and you would get stuck there ⟦41⟧.
strings.city.3.list.3: An amber signal does not mean “I’ll make it”, it means “I prepare to stop”.
strings.city.3.list.4: As you turn, take one more look at the pedestrian crossing at the last moment.
strings.city.4.p.0: Roundabouts in Kazakhstan’s cities can be large and multi-lane. The main thing is to work out in advance who gives way to whom: look at the priority signs before the entrance, where most often there is the “Give way” sign.
strings.city.4.list.0: Slow down before entering and find a gap in the traffic.
strings.city.4.list.1: If your exit is close, keep to the right lane; if it is far, or you are making a U-turn, take your lane in advance according to the markings and signs.
strings.city.4.list.2: Inside the roundabout, watch the cars on your right and left: many change lanes at the last moment.
strings.city.4.list.3: Before your exit, switch on the right indicator and move to the right in advance.
strings.city.4.list.4: If you miss your exit, go round once more, and do not brake on the roundabout.
strings.city.5.p.0: At an uncontrolled crossing, you give way to pedestrians crossing the road (para. 106 of the Rules). If a car in the adjacent lane has stopped before the crossing, continue only after making sure there are no people beyond it ⟦42⟧.
strings.city.5.list.0: Approaching a crossing, take your foot off the accelerator and watch the pavements, not just the crossing itself.
strings.city.5.list.1: Always let a pedestrian with a white cane cross ⟦43⟧.
strings.city.5.list.2: Near stops, schools, markets and shopping centres, people appear unexpectedly, including away from crossings.
strings.city.5.list.3: In winter, pedestrians in hoods hear and see poorly, and on ice they cannot stop quickly.
strings.city.5.list.4: In the evening, people in dark clothes are seen very late: slow down near crossings.
strings.city.6.p.0: In built-up areas, you give way to buses and trolleybuses moving off from a marked stop (para. 127 of the Rules). You must not drive or stop in a lane for route vehicles, except in cases the Rules allow, for example to turn ⟦44⟧.
strings.city.6.list.0: When passing a stationary bus, remember that someone may step out from behind it. Give way to those walking to or from the bus ⟦45⟧.
strings.city.6.list.1: A bus has switched on its left indicator at a stop: let it pull out.
strings.city.6.list.2: Taxis and cars with passengers stop suddenly: keep your distance and do not tailgate.
strings.city.6.list.3: Do not overtake a bus on the right at a stop.
strings.city.6.list.4: Near vehicles displaying the “Carriage of children” sign, slow down and let children pass ⟦46⟧.
strings.city.7.p.0: At night you see less and later. Choose your speed according to visibility (para. 72 of the Rules).
strings.city.7.list.0: Switch from main beam to dipped headlights at least 150 m before an oncoming car, and always when the main beam could dazzle others ⟦47⟧.
strings.city.7.list.1: If you are dazzled, switch on the hazard warning lights and, without changing lane, stop ⟦48⟧.
strings.city.7.list.2: Do not look straight at oncoming headlights, look towards the right edge of the road.
strings.city.7.list.3: Keep your headlights and windows clean, including on the inside: dirt increases glare.
strings.city.7.list.4: If you are tired, driving at night is twice as dangerous. Stop and rest.
strings.city.8.p.0: The first minutes of rain are the slipperiest: water mixes with dust and oil on the asphalt. Braking distance gets longer and visibility gets worse.
strings.city.8.list.0: Slow down smoothly and increase your following distance to 3-4 seconds.
strings.city.8.list.1: Switch on dipped headlights so that you can be seen.
strings.city.8.list.2: If the windows mist up, turn on the windscreen demister and, if necessary, the air conditioning.
strings.city.8.list.3: Avoid deep puddles if it is safe, or drive through them slowly: there may be a pothole in the puddle.
strings.city.8.list.4: If the steering feels light and the car “floats”, that is aquaplaning: ease off the accelerator smoothly, hold the wheel straight and do not brake hard.
strings.city.9.p.0: In many regions of Kazakhstan winter is long: severe frosts, blizzards and snowdrifts on highways, and black ice when the temperature is around zero. In winter the car brakes worse and skids easily.
strings.city.9.p.1: You must not mix studded and non-studded tyres, or frost-resistant and non-frost-resistant tyres, on the same axle ⟦49⟧. Winter tyres grip noticeably better in cold and snow.
strings.city.9.list.0: Before setting off, clear snow and ice from all windows, mirrors, headlights and the roof.
strings.city.9.list.1: Make every action smooth: accelerator, brake, steering. Sudden movements on ice almost always lead to a skid.
strings.city.9.list.2: Following distance: several times more than in summer.
strings.city.9.list.3: Black ice appears first on bridges, flyovers, in the shade and near water.
strings.city.9.list.4: On an empty stretch with no cars behind you, brake lightly to feel how slippery it is.
strings.city.9.list.5: If the rear axle skids, steer in the direction of the skid and straighten the wheels as soon as the car starts to go straight.
strings.city.9.list.6: On a highway in a blizzard, traffic may be organised in a convoy: the convoy leader sets the speed and distance, and overtaking inside the convoy is not allowed (Chapter 26 of the Rules).
strings.city.9.list.7: Do not go out on the highway in a snowstorm unless absolutely necessary. Take warm clothes, water and a full tank.
strings.city.10.p.0: Until you have your licence, you may drive on roads only with an instructor (para. 147 of the Rules). So your first solo drives are a separate stage, and it is worth preparing for it.
strings.city.10.list.0: Start with familiar routes and quiet times: weekend mornings, not the rush hour.
strings.city.10.list.1: Plan your route in advance and set up the navigation before you start driving.
strings.city.10.list.2: It is handy to make the first drives with an experienced driver beside you, who will advise you without fussing.
strings.city.10.list.3: Phone in a holder, calls only through a headset or hands-free ⟦50⟧.
strings.city.10.list.4: Do not give in to horns behind you and do not try to “keep up with the flow”. Your speed is the one at which you control everything.
strings.city.10.list.5: Try difficult situations (narrow yards, parking at shopping centres, multi-lane interchanges) at quiet times first.
strings.city.11.p.0: Anyone can stall, especially in a manual car. It is unpleasant but not dangerous if you act calmly.
strings.city.11.list.0: Press the brake, press the clutch, select neutral.
strings.city.11.list.1: On a slope, apply the handbrake so that you do not roll back.
strings.city.11.list.2: Start the engine and move off as usual, without hurrying.
strings.city.11.list.3: If you cannot restart quickly, switch on the hazard warning lights to warn others.
strings.city.11.list.4: At an intersection, ignore horns behind you: a couple of extra seconds are better than a new mistake.
strings.city.11.list.5: If you stall on a level crossing, immediately get the passengers out and clear the crossing by any means.
